scope: Bounded review of ISO 32000-2:2020(E) §§9.6.2.3, 9.6.4 Type 3 entries relevant to glyph sizing/width/bounds and §9.6.5.3, including only directly relevant EC3 corrections. Not whole-clause certification.

features.title: Type 3 code-to-name mapping and required Encoding form
features.source: Primary Table 110, physical p.333 / printed p.318, requires /Encoding to be a dictionary. §9.6.5.3, physical p.348 / printed p.333, says the code-to-glyph-name mapping is entirely defined by that entry and Type 3 has no default glyph name. §9.6.4 steps a-b say obtain the name from Encoding, then paint nothing when CharProcs lacks the key.
features.errata: No direct EC3 amendment to §9.6.5.3 found in the inspected EC3 transcription. EC3 #111 edits §9.6.4 glyph descriptions from streams to objects and adds NOTE 2 on operator categories; unrelated to Encoding form. EC3 #128 changes glyph Resources lookup, also unrelated to mapping.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.6.5.3 (implemented), code crates/pdf-model/src/type3.rs; ledger links tests in crates/pdf-model/tests/type3.rs and type3_residual_audit.rs. The ledger note incorrectly says a direct named Encoding is permitted for Type 3 based on §9.6.5.1; Table 110's more specific required dictionary form makes those tests tolerance evidence only.
features.implementation: Type3Font::read parses an Encoding dictionary and Differences; Type3Font::glyph maps the byte through the resulting code/name map then looks up CharProcs. Missing name/key returns no glyph, as §9.6.4 step b specifies. Direct names are also accepted as a reader extension in type3.rs.
features.assertions: The default public Fixture in tests/type3.rs has an exact xref, required Encoding dictionary object with Differences [97 /square /triangle], matching CharProcs, FirstChar/LastChar/Widths, and distinct painted glyphs. type3_residual_audit.rs::an_encoding_omission_does_not_select_notdef_or_another_charproc exercises an omitted code with distinguishable /.notdef and other CharProcs and asserts no fallback. Three named-Encoding tests instead use a direct name; they assert current permissive/refusal behavior on producer-invalid Type 3 dictionaries and must be labelled tolerance/report-policy tests, never valid-input conformance.
features.verdict: Conforming dictionary mapping and no-default behavior have direct implementation and public assertion evidence in sampled paths. No new reader behavior defect identified. Existing named Encoding assertions overstate normative validity unless labelled as tolerance behavior.
features.residuals: No exhaustive malformed Encoding policy or all Differences array forms audited. Table 110 requires dictionary producer form; the standard does not thereby require a reader to reject or accept the malformed direct-name form.

features.title: Glyph-space widths, FontMatrix and horizontal text advance
features.source: Table 110, physical p.333 / printed p.318, places Type 3 Widths in glyph space interpreted by FontMatrix; if the matrix rotates, only the horizontal component of transformed width is used; codes outside FirstChar..LastChar have width zero. §9.2.4 requires an explicit FontMatrix for Type 3.
features.errata: EC3 #43 corrects Table 111 operand-label grammar, not this width rule. EC3 #144 corrects §9.6.4's example LastChar from 104 to 98; the public fixture uses 98. No inspected EC3 change alters the width/matrix rule.
features.ledger: §9.6.4 row in doc/conformance/ledger.toml; implementation crates/pdf-model/src/type3.rs::Type3Font::advance and read; public tests type3.rs::a_width_advances_through_the_font_matrix and type3_spec_audit.rs rotated-matrix case; internal unit type3.rs::a_width_is_read_through_the_font_matrix.
features.implementation: advance indexes the declared widths from FirstChar, defaults to zero outside the vector, and multiplies by FontMatrix.a. Glyph rendering composes font matrix with text transform. A noninvertible present FontMatrix is rejected by the model; the bounded tests cover zero-matrix rationale and rotated horizontal advance.
features.assertions: The public two-glyph test observes the second glyph's position: width 1000 at size 10 moves 10 with matrix .001 and 100 with matrix .01. Internal test separately compares widths 1 under unit and .001 matrices and checks both adjacent out-of-range codes are zero. Rotation test checks that advance remains horizontal and includes a scale control.
features.verdict: Good independent public geometry assertion plus direct model unit evidence for the sampled advance rule. No gap found in these cases.
features.residuals: No independent audit of every malformed width-array shape or affine matrix family. These tests do not certify all Table 110 entries.

features.title: FontBBox and glyph d1 bounding boxes describe mark extents
features.source: Table 110 FontBBox is the font's glyph-space bounding box enclosing marks; when nonzero it is to be accurate. Table 111 d1 bbox likewise describes glyph marks. Both tables state that marks outside the stated box make behavior implementation-dependent. They do not impose a reader clipping rule.
features.errata: EC3 #43 makes operand labels grammatical; no substantive change to the bounds. EC3 #111 adds NOTE 2 that any operator category is available subject to this clause's restrictions.
features.ledger: §9.6.4 Type 3 row; implementation crates/pdf-model/src/type3.rs and content/text/type3.rs. Public assertions are in crates/pdf-model/tests/type3.rs.
features.implementation: Normal Type 3 glyph painting does not clip marks to FontBBox or d1's bbox. FontBBox is used as a glyph extent in specific downstream paths (for example redaction), while display-list rendering follows glyph operators. This behavior is compatible with the source's explicit implementation-dependent result for out-of-box marks.
features.assertions: Existing test an_uncoloured_glyph_that_fills_and_strokes_uses_both_inherited_colours declares [0 0 750 750] in both font and d1 bounds but strokes the same rectangle with 72-unit width, yielding extents [-36,-36]..[786,786] (square miter joins). Existing inline-image d0 test maps a unit image square by [750 0 200 375 0 0], reaching x=950; the other glyph reaches y=750. Its original FontBBox stopped at 750 in x. The scratch patch corrects these producer fixtures; width stays 1000, and exact xref/no-recovery assertion is added to the fixture helper.
features.verdict: No renderer defect follows from the old test bounds: their behavior is implementation-dependent under the standard. Patch corrects fixture claims so those tests exercise valid reported bounds. It does not assert clipping or behavior outside bounds.
features.residuals: The original d1 case also tests fill/stroke color behavior, not bound enforcement. The new image FontBBox encloses both glyphs ([0 0 950 750]); the stroked glyph box is [-36 -36 786 786]. No assertion requires an implementation to clip to either bounds field.

features.title: Multiple master Type 1 instances
features.source: Primary §9.6.2.3, physical p.315 / printed p.300: MMType1 instances use the Type 1 dictionary entries with /Subtype MMType1; embedded instance is an ordinary Type 1 font program. BaseFont space-to-underscore convention is expressly not prescribed by this specification.
features.errata: No directly applicable EC3 amendment identified in the inspected clause. Nearby #47/#48 concern §9.6.2.1 standard-14 availability, not MMType1 instance semantics.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.6.2.3 says loader does not branch on simple-font subtype and records the ordinary Type 1 program route; BaseFont naming convention is not prescribed.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/loading.rs simple-font route selects Type 3/Type 0 specially, then loads other simple font programs through the Type 1/TrueType program selection path; no MMType1-specific program parser or BaseFont instance-name parser was found.
features.assertions: Ledger test a_simple_fonts_subtype_selects_nothing feeds the same deliberately invalid program bytes to Type1, MMType1 and TrueType and compares failure route; it tests dispatch, not a successful MMType1 instance. No successful embedded MMType1 instance test found in the bounded search.
features.verdict: Implementation route is consistent with snapshot instance being an ordinary Type 1 program; no evidence of a functional gap. Current test is narrowly a dispatch test, so ledger wording must not imply successful MMType1 fixture conformance coverage.
features.residuals: No successful real MMType1 instance/program test was added: obtaining a conforming embedded fixture is beyond this bounded shard. The spec does not mandate parsing the non-prescribed BaseFont naming convention.

features.title: Reuse of Type 3 glyph descriptions
features.source: The audited ISO requirements specify glyph streams and their execution, not a Type 3-specific glyph cache.
features.ledger: Cache statement is in ADR 0018/0427, not a normative requirement row.
features.implementation: Nested glyph streams use Document's decoded stream cache through the same content stream path; no separate Type 3 glyph-result cache was found.
features.assertions: Generic decoded-stream memo tests measure repeated decode and charging, not a Type 3 glyph raster cache.
features.verdict: No conformance gap: cache strategy is an implementation choice and relevant bounded ADR rationale remains plausible.
features.residuals: No performance benchmark repeated; outside normative audit scope.
